output.title: When rounding becomes a workflow problem
output.body:
If “rounding claims” keeps coming up as a vague complaint, it is usually not a math problem first. It is a workflow problem: somewhere in your business, two numbers are close enough to be annoying, and someone has to decide whether the gap matters.

That could be an invoice total, a currency conversion, a timesheet variance, or an estimate-versus-actual mismatch. The useful question is: which recurring workflow forces you to compare two slightly different numbers and make a judgment call?

Then draw the control boundary. Which cases are already policy, like rounding to the nearest cent? Which ones need human judgment, like anything above your own threshold? Which ones have no rule at all? If the difference is invisible and acceptable, it can stay background noise. If it affects approval or audit notes, it needs an explicit human step.

The practical next step is to write one plain-English rule for one recurring workflow. For example: “Round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” Then ask yourself: do I already document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly yet, fix the policy first. The spreadsheet can wait; it usually does.
